name: Integrative, Comparative and Marine Biology, Ph.D.
department: Department of Biology and Marine Biology

deadline.value: Fall 2027 application deadline is February 1, 2027 (Spring 2027: November 1, 2026; Summer 2027 Sessions 1 & 2: February 1, 2027). Teaching assistantship applications are due February 15.

also.quote: The deadline for applying, if you wish to have a teaching assistantship, is February 15.

gre_general.value: GRE General Test is not required for admission to the Ph.D. in Integrative, Comparative and Marine Biology.
gre_general.quote: NOTE: The Graduate Record of Examination (GRE) General Test is not required for admission.

gre_subject.value: No GRE Subject Test exists for Biology (ETS discontinued the GRE Biology Test in May 2021; department FAQ also states the Biology subject GRE is not required).
gre_subject.quote: The GRE Biology Test and the GRE Literature in English Test were discontinued in May 2021.

also.quote: The Biology subject GRE is not required.

supervisor.value: Applicants must contact prospective faculty and secure acceptance/sponsorship into a faculty advisor's research group to be admitted.
supervisor.quote: The applicant must secure a position in a faculty advisor’s research group in order to be admitted into the program.

also.quote: Students who are not selected by a faculty member for a position in their lab will not be accepted into the program.

funding.value: Department offers competitive Teaching Assistantships ($21,000 for the 9-month academic year paid over 10 months, normally renewed for 4 years with satisfactory performance, Feb 15 request deadline) and faculty-grant Research Assistantships (doctoral GRAs receive full NC Resident + Non-Resident tuition support per Graduate School policy), subject to funding availability.
funding.quote: The Department of Biology and Marine Biology offers teaching assistantships to students enrolled in the Biology Master's and Marine Biology Master's and Ph.D. programs based on the continued availability of funding. | Teaching assistantships are currently valued at $13,000 for the 9-month academic year for Master's students and $21,000 for the 9-month academic year for Ph.D. students but are paid over 10 months.

also.quote: Teaching assistantships are awarded for one academic year. Master's students may normally expect to be continued for a second year and Ph.D. students for four years if performance is satisfactory.

Graduate Research Assistants receive tuition support in addition to their monthly stipend. Students enrolled in master's programs will receive the equivalent of the NC Resident (In-State) portion of their tuition, while students enrolled in doctoral programs will receive both the NC Resident and NC Non-Resident portions of their tuition.

entry_route.value: Admits applicants directly with a four-year bachelor's degree in biology or related discipline (>= 3.0 GPA, 60 post-baccalaureate credit hours); prior M.S. holders may count up to 30 credit hours toward the doctorate.
entry_route.quote: A bachelor’s degree in biology or a related discipline from an accredited U.S. college or university or its equivalent at an international institution based on a four-year program. | Degree Requirements (60 post-baccalaureate credit hours) | The maximum amount of credit that a Ph.D. student may count toward a doctorate from a master’s degree program is 30 credit hours.

notes: DHS STEM-designated Ph.D. (CIP 26.9999 Biological and Biomedical Sciences, Other). Teaching assistantships require IELTS 7.0 (vs 6.5 for admission) or speaking proficiency if international. Slate also notes M.S. students may apply to transition after their first year.
